2. The suit land originally belonged to one Protab Chandra Dhali and others. Protab Chandra transferred the suit land to one Darika Nath the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered sale deed on 9th Magh, 1323 B. S. and Darika Nath purchased the same with his own money and for his own benefit; that Darika Nath died leaving plaintiff No. 1 and father of plaintiff No. 2; At the time of R. S. operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of Darika Nath, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-4 and some of the defendants; the predecessors of defendants one third share in the name of Darika Nath recorded in the name of Darika Nath alone. Manik Meah and Gour Charan or their heirs defendants No. 1-9 have no right, title and interest or possession in the suit land. Plaintiff No. 1 and father of plaintiff No. 2 transferred 1/4 bigha of lands to Sasti Charan predecessor of defendants 15-17 with an agreement of reconvcyance. The name of defendants 1, 2, 5 and 6 were also mentioned in the Patta as the executants and Sasti Charan in collusion on with defendants 1, 2, 5 and 6 inserted 3 bighas of land in the patta. But the suit land was under the possession of the plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiff returned the consideration money to the patta, 20/25 years back to defendants 15-17 and the defendants returned the original patta to the plaintiffs. The original patta has been lost at the time of liberation. The suit land has been wrongly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-9. 

 5. The positive case of defendants 10-14 in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Dwarika Nath Bjswas and his brother, that Owarika Nath died leaving two sons plaintiff No. 1 and father of plaintiff No. 2; that the two Sons of Dwarika Nath and their co-sharers settled the suit, land measuring an area of 1.56 acres to Sasti Charan father of defendants 15- 17 by registered patta dated 16.12.48 and Sasti Charan paid rent. Sasti Charan allowed the possession of the suit land and the suit land is wrongly recorded in his name in A. Khatian and after his death his three Sons defendant Nos. 15-17 transferred the suit land to defendant Nos. 10-14 by their registered kabia dated 29.6.76 and the defendants Nos. 10-14 have been possessing the suit land. Defendant Nos. 15-17 never returned the original patta to the plaintiffs. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Perused the judgments of the learned courts below and considered the evidence on record. It appears that the learned trial court has considered the case from all angles and rightly held that the suit was not maintainable. On the question of limitation also the trial court found that the plaintiffs being fully aware of the preparation of revisional survey record ever since 16-1248 with reference to which the state acquisition record was prepared the suit filed on 10.5.83 was barred by limitation. The learned trial court also found that the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest & possession over the suit land. The learned lower appellate court in reversing the decision of the learned trial court has not considered all these different aspects of the case. The only point that was taken up by the learned lower appellate court is whether the judgment and decree of the trial court is sustainable. In order to come to that decision all the issues framed, discussed and decided by the learned trial court against the plaintiff required careful consideration with reference to the materials on record, because if any single issue goes against the plaintiff, the decision of the trial court becomes sustainable as each & every issue framed in the suit is the basic issue going at the root of the suit itself. The finding of the learned lower appellate court that the suit land was not delivered to Satish Charan is abrupt without any reference to evidence, similarly the finding that the patta was not acted upon is also without any reference to evidence and as such the finding that Satish Charan did not acquire any title has no leg to stand. The learned lower appellate court has also not recorded any finding as to limitation which was found against the plaintiffs by the learned trial court referring to the evidence. The finding of the lower appellate court that the state acquisition record is wrong has no bais and this finding by itself cannot save the limitation. So considering all these facts & circumstances I am of the opinion that the judgment and decree of the learned lower appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal.
